title: workflow-pattern-v1
description: Machine-readable contract for a workflow-pattern-v1 document (spec/workflow-pattern-v1.md). A pattern is a small directed graph of nodes and edges: each node is a durable-boundary execution contract (kind, role, inputs, outputs, evidence, effects, budget, outcomes); `risk-input` maps a risk-class verdict to the mandatory gate nodes it requires; `join` names the node carrying the integration check. This contract is DESCRIPTIVE of the per-file, frontmatter-shape rules only: required keys, field types, and closed value sets. It deliberately does NOT encode the cross-field rules `statusgen patterns --lint` owns (a node's effect kind must be permitted for its role; a node whose evidence includes `review` must have a role distinct from every node that produced its inputs; `join` must name a `check` node) — those need the pattern's own edges and node graph resolved, which a per-value schema cannot express. Where the two would disagree the schema is the LOOSER of the two on purpose.

schema.description: The opt-in schema marker. Its presence is what selects a file for validation; for this contract it is exactly workflow-pattern-v1.

version.description: Bumped on every node/edge/evidence edit after the pattern's first review.

risk-input.description: Risk-class verdict to mandatory gate-node-id list. All four verdicts MUST be present — a pattern that does not state what an `elevated` or `human` risk class requires cannot be instantiated against one. Presence of all four keys is a MUST-rule the lint checks against the resolved document (`pattern-risk-input-missing-verdict`), not a schema `required` list here, so a missing verdict is reported as a MUST-rule violation, distinct from a shape violation, per spec/workflow-pattern-v1.md §8.2.

nodes.description: The pattern's node set. Every node sits at a durable boundary (an artifact, an independent check, a human decision, an external effect) — a step that produces none of these is not a node.

id.description: The node's identity within this pattern. Referenced by edges, `join`, `risk-input` gate lists and other nodes' `effects[].target`.

kind.description: Exactly one node kind. `artifact` produces a durable output; `check` is an independent verification (review or verify); `decision` is a human or desk disposition; `effect` performs an action with external consequence.

role.description: A topology role, or human for an effect-free decision only. Human binds no actor or capability; its decision is an external authenticated act.

inputs.description: What this node needs before it can run. `artifact` names the artifact kind it consumes; `revision` optionally pins which revision (e.g. `brief.version`).

outputs.description: The durable artifacts this node produces, by name. An `effects[].target` naming one of these is how the node's own effects stay owned by its own output.

evidence.description: The claims this node owes, each in words a verifier can check.

signal.description: kind: observe ONLY — the named signal watched over `window` after a change lands (e.g. an error-rate metric, an alert). Meaningless for any other kind; a conforming implementation declares `observe` only where a deploy exists (spec/workflow-pattern-v1.md §4.1) — where none exists the kind is omitted, never recorded with these fields empty as "n/a".

band.description: kind: observe ONLY — the acceptable range/threshold the signal must stay within for the claim to resolve `pass` (e.g. "error rate < 1%").

window.description: kind: observe ONLY — how long after the change lands the signal is watched (e.g. "PT1H", "24h").

source.description: kind: observe ONLY — where the coverage rule reads the signal FROM. An unreadable source resolves the claim to could-not-check, never pass (graph-execution/03).

effects.description: External-consequence actions this node performs. The lint's `pattern-effect-exceeds-role` rule refuses a node whose effect kind is not permitted for its role (spec/workflow-pattern-v1.md §4's role-to-effect-kind table).

kind.description: A closed set: the union of the effect kinds spec/workflow-pattern-v1.md §7's role table grants. An unknown kind fails this shape check independently of `pattern-effect-exceeds-role`, which then decides whether the node's role holds it. A signal pattern's containment steps are not effects of this list; they live in `containment.steps` (graph-execution/08).

outcomes.description: Non-success dispositions this node may end in.

signal.description: graph-execution/08, OPTIONAL. Declared by the first node of a signal-instantiated pattern: the instance fields a signal must carry, the hold on a could-not-check liveness reading, the signal classes, and per-class run admission (spec/workflow-pattern-v1.md §4.3).

containment.description: graph-execution/08, OPTIONAL. The closed containment taxonomy a signal node may choose from, or the recorded outcome `none-needed` with the signal reading that justifies it. Permitted only on the node that declares `signal` (pattern-effect-exceeds-role).

routes.description: graph-execution/08, OPTIONAL. A selector decision node's exits: signal or culprit class to the node id that class routes to.

culprit.description: graph-execution/08, OPTIONAL. The gate-red class's culprit record a confirm node owes, its conservative default class, and the gates that withhold their detail by design.

remedies.description: graph-execution/08, OPTIONAL. The mechanical exit's closed remedy set on the culprit file, the gate-configuration paths it refuses, and the node a refused remedy routes to.

default.description: graph-execution/08, OPTIONAL. The recommended default next step a human decision carries. REQUIRED (pattern-judgement-no-default) on the node a gate-red judgement route names.

join.description: The node id carrying the integration check. MUST name a `check`-kind node (`statusgen patterns --lint`'s `pattern-join-not-check` rule).

limits.description: graph-execution/08, OPTIONAL; REQUIRED when a node's signal declares the gate-red class (pattern-gate-red-incomplete). One open artifact per culprit, an open-artifact ceiling and a per-window rate, each failing closed to an escalation signal.
